capability: Compile a restricted density expression into value and analytic first-derivative callables.
operation: compile an analytic density and its derivative callable
discovery.boundary: Only the restricted analytic expression syntax is supported.

title.zh: 安全解析密度与链式法则求导

summary: Compile a restricted density expression into value and analytic first-derivative callables.

identity.definition: Parse finite real constants, pi, v, arithmetic and the declared elementary functions; propagate pairs (value, derivative) by exact analytic chain rules. MATLAB elementwise operators are normalized before parsing.
identity.coordinates: Dimensionless real velocity and complex phase or frequency
identity.boundary: Only the restricted analytic expression syntax is supported.
assumptions: Density is real and integrable on the real contour.
No collective-mode uniqueness or certified global quadrature bound is asserted.
Expression has a valid analytic extension where continuation is requested.
Explicit increasing mesh resolves all density features and tails.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: Analytic density in v using finite real constants, pi, arithmetic and exp/log/sqrt/sin/cos/sinh/cosh/tanh; MATLAB point operators accepted.
inputs.constraints: Real integrable density with decaying derivative; no arbitrary code, comparisons, attributes or indexing.

outputs.name: return
outputs.description: DensityExpression instance. Calling instance(v) returns f(v); instance.derivative(v) returns analytic df/dv for scalar or NumPy-array real/complex v.
outputs.constraints: Arithmetic and domain constraints of the entered expression apply.

supported: Safe AST expression parsing, MATLAB point-operator normalization, analytic first derivatives and real/complex scalar or array evaluations.
excluded: Arbitrary code, attributes, indexing, comparisons and piecewise expressions.
Symbolic simplification or guarantees of integrability.
preconditions: Expression syntax is restricted to the declared arithmetic/functions.
Evaluation points lie in a finite domain where the entered expression and derivative are representable.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for unsupported AST nodes, non-finite constants, malformed expressions, or non-numeric velocity values.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: NumPy overflow/invalid arithmetic propagates; no symbolic recovery or value repair is attempted.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; parsing, evaluation and analytic differentiation are non-iterative.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial value or derivative is returned; the expression is parsed before evaluation.

scope: Lorentzian values and derivatives at real/complex points.
Explicit rejection of attributes, arbitrary calls, unknown names, indexing, lists and booleans.
known_limitations: This parser does not prove integrability, positivity, normalization or analytic continuation validity.
Arithmetic exceptions and nonfinite expression evaluations are not converted into symbolic diagnoses.
Only shared-file coverage is bound (test_generalized_dispersion_models.py); no asset-specific failure/limit probe is recorded.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to the declared relation: Parse finite real constants, pi, v, arithmetic and the declared elementary functions; propagate pairs (value, derivative) by exact analytic chain rules. MATLAB elementwise operators are normalized before parsing. Evidence: test_generalized_dispersion_models.py (14 recorded test functions; shared-file coverage only; self-consistency/regression only); the contract example ran. Excluded scope: Arbitrary code, attributes, indexing, comparisons and piecewise expressions; Symbolic simplification or guarantees of integrability.

example.description: Compile a Lorentzian expression and compare its value and derivative with closed forms.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic.generalized_dispersion import DensityExpression
f=DensityExpression('1./(1+v.^2)/pi')
v=.7
assert abs(f(v)-1/(1+v*v)/np.pi)<1e-14
assert abs(f.derivative(v)+2*v/(1+v*v)**2/np.pi)<1e-14
example.expected: Observed PASS: the compiled Lorentzian value and analytic derivative agree with their closed forms at v=0.7.

references: Hua-Sheng Xie, Generalized plasma dispersion function, Phys. Plasmas. 20 (2013), 092125 (scientific context)
